narrative.overview: node-dev-host does its real work out of sight. A container copies a project, builds it, and serves it with Caddy, and you never open a window onto any of that. The control dashboard is the only place the work becomes visible. It is the product's observation deck, not an admin extra. If a build fails, a refresh stalls, or a container sits in `unknown`, the dashboard is the single surface that tells you, so the whole design is arranged to make that answer readable at a glance.
keyCharacteristics: State first: build state, freshness and health are the loudest things on screen; actions are the quietest.
Neutral by default, colour only as signal. Three hues, each tied to one meaning.
Every status is carried by a word as well as a colour, so it survives colour blindness and greyscale.
The panel reports on itself: last-refresh time, refreshing indicator, stale warning, read-only mode.
Flat and calm. Depth is a hairline border; motion is limited to the refresh spinner and state transitions.
Same hierarchy on a wide table and on a phone-width stacked card.

rules.name: The Three Signals Rule
rules.body: Green, blue and red each mean one thing: ok, building, failed. No other element on the dashboard may use those hues.

rules.name: The Word Beside the Colour Rule
rules.body: A status is never colour alone. Every badge prints its state name.

rules.name: The Quiet Normal Rule
rules.body: The healthy path is the quietest. Only `failed` and a stale refresh are allowed to raise the visual volume.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Ports, counts and times use fixed-width figures so a polled value changing does not shift the layout.

rules.name: The One Title Rule
rules.body: The page has one heading. Hierarchy below it comes from weight, colour and position.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Nothing on the data surface casts a shadow.

dos: Do lead every container row with state: the build badge and the last-build time are the first things a scan should land on after the name.
Do print the state name inside every status badge (The Word Beside the Colour Rule).
Do show the panel's own health in the header: last update time, refreshing indicator, read-only mode.
Do keep the last good data on screen when a refresh fails, and put the stale alert above it.
Do show `unknown` or an em dash when a value cannot be read. Never invent a state, never leave a blank cell.
Do keep layout stable across polls: fixed-width figures, content-driven widths, rows keyed by container id.
Do keep Logs reachable in every mode, including read-only and for stopped containers.
Do keep the status hues to their three meanings (green ok, blue building, red failed) in both themes.
Do check any new status colour in light and dark for 4.5:1 text contrast before shipping it.
donts: Don't use green, blue or red for decoration, links, hover states or branding.
Don't communicate a state by colour alone, or by an icon without a word.
Don't hide, collapse or silently clear failure information.
Don't add a hero, a marketing banner, illustrations or large decorative empty space above the table.
Don't add shadows, gradients or glass effects to the data surface.
Don't reorder rows or reflow columns when data refreshes.
Don't colour the Docker container state badge.
Don't add a custom font, a second accent colour or a bespoke component where a shadcn primitive already fits.
